summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood AE/SE and LumenForge partnership and cloud infra teams. Discussed go-to-market alignment, technical compatibility for co-hosted inference, regions, and security/compliance requirements. Agreed to follow up with benchmarks and a technical deep-dive.
topics: Commercial models and referral / reseller mechanics
Next steps: deck, benchmarks, technical deep-dive
transcript: [00:00] Sofia Kline: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm sofia from redwood, i'm the ae on the partnerships team. we have ravi and maya with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Daniel Ortega: good, thanks. excited to learn more about how redwood might fit with lumenforge offerings, thanks for setting this up.
[00:15] Priya Nair: hi all, priya here. we'll probably lean on ravi for the infra questions, and elena for security stuff.

[00:23] Sofia Kline: great. quick agenda - we'll do a 10 minute partner intro from redwood, then we want to understand lumenforge's capacity, regions, and partner goals; finally talk technical touch points like vpc, kms, and deployments. sound ok?
[00:36] Jake Morales: yes sounds good. timeline wise lumenforge is exploring partnerships to expand our marketplace by q2, looking for partners who can integrate quickly.

[00:45] Ravi Patel: quick context from redwood - we provide an inference platform for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. main differentiators are latency/cost controls, smart routing, and a unified API across deployment modes. we typically work with partners who want to offer managed inference or co-sell dedicated capacity. (short pause)
[01:10] Elena Wu: could you clarify "dedicated" - is that like reserved gpu pools that you run in the partner datacenter?

[01:18] Ravi Patel: yeah exactly. dedicated can be hosted in our cloud or deployed in partner-managed infrastructure depending on contract. for private deployments we support vpc peering and an on-prem package; key management hooks are via customer kms/hsm, and we emit audit logs. sorry - kms, not ksm.
[01:35] Priya Nair: that's helpful. what scheduling/placement control do you need? we run multi-tenant racks and sometimes have tenancy or pinning requirements for enterprise customers.

[01:44] Ravi Patel: we expose placement preferences in the deployment config. you can pin model instances to specific GPU pools or racks, and we support autoscaling policies with burst capacity. for networking we prefer vpc peering and IPSec. we also support model pinning to avoid cross-tenant eviction in noisy-neighbor scenarios.
[02:10] Daniel Ortega: commercial question - are you looking for resellers or referral partners?

[02:15] Sofia Kline: good q. our partner program has both tracks. for a partner like lumenforge we'd probably discuss co-selling and reseller options - basic revenue share + technical enablement. i'll send the partner one-pager after this call.
[02:28] Jake Morales: great. on the technical side, what model families and quantization formats do you support? we have customers asking about fp16 and int8 and even newer quant formats.

[02:36] Ravi Patel: we support float16, int8 quantized runtimes, and some 4-bit quant variants depending on model. we also do kernel selection at compile time and have execution paths optimized per architecture. important note: some older quant formats might need a small tuning pass. we've seen typical perf wins of 2-3x with int8 on sequence models.
[03:05] Priya Nair: latency SLOs - what should we expect for 8k context chat models?

[03:11] Ravi Patel: for 8k, hosted endpoints 95th perc latency is typically ~200-400ms token generation depending on batch size and hardware. on dedicated A100 or H100 pools, you can get lower latency but it depends on batching profiles. we can share perf profiles for our curated models.
[03:30] Elena Wu: security - do you support customer-managed keys and isolated control planes? we need to know for SOC2 and some regulated customers.

[03:38] Maya Chen: yes. for private deployments the control plane can be customer-hosted in their vpc, and we integrate with KMS/HSM. we also provide audit logs, RBAC, and SAML/SSO integrations. we can share SOC2 artifacts under NDA. (interrupt)
[03:55] Daniel Ortega: that was one of our hard requirements. good to hear. how do you handle data residency / logging?

[04:03] Ravi Patel: logs and telemetry can be shipped to customer-managed sinks. we also provide an option to disable persistent logging for sensitive workloads; request and response payload handling is configurable per deployment. but we do need some minimal telemetry for operational health unless otherwise negotiated.
[04:25] Priya Nair: networking again - VPC peering or private link? what's empirically easier to set up for partners?

[04:32] Ravi Patel: VPC peering is straightforward for many partners; for marketplace integrations private link or partner interconnects are common. we adapt to partner networking patterns - on-prem sometimes uses ipsec tunnels. we'll need a runbook though.
[04:50] Jake Morales: do you have an SDK or operators you'd want partners to run?

[04:55] Sofia Kline: we have SDKs and a small operator for lifecycle hooks for private deployments. for marketplace integrations we also provide dockerized runtime images and helm charts. we'll share the repo links.
[05:08] Daniel Ortega: commercial again - pricing model for partners, do you provide committed discounts for resellers?
[05:14] Sofia Kline: yes committed reserved capacity has discounts. for reseller deals we can discuss MSRP and partner margins; we'll include typical discount tiers in the partner doc.
[05:25] Priya Nair: on benchmarking - if we wanted to co-host instances, what would you need from our side?

[05:30] Ravi Patel: ideal is GPU inventory (model, VRAM), region/az, NIC bandwidth, and available kernel/driver versions. from there we pick a few representative models - e.g., a 7b chat model, 30b decoder, and an embedding model - and run throughput/latency runs. we typically ask for access to a small test pool for ~48-72 hours.
[05:55] Elena Wu: any regulatory blockers for Europe region?

[06:00] Maya Chen: we have EU regions and data residency options; the main item is contractual data processing addendums and SCCs - we can route to partner-run infra in eu and ensure GDPR controls. we'll share our DPA template.
[06:12] Daniel Ortega: what's the onboarding timeline if we decide to pilot?

[06:16] Sofia Kline: for a pilot with a dedicated pool usually 3-6 weeks: contract + SOW 1-2 weeks, provisioning and networking 1-2 weeks, and pilot tuning + benchmarks 1-2 weeks. faster if partner already has infra and we use a hosted operator install.
[06:33] Jake Morales: okay. do you have any existing marketplace integrations or joint customers?
[06:38] Sofia Kline: yes we have a few gpu host partners and have done co-sell with select partners; i'll include anonymized case studies in the deck. apologies for the timestamp glitch there.
[06:48] Priya Nair: what are typical failures you've seen in partner setups?

[06:52] Ravi Patel: common issues are driver mismatches, insufficient NIC bandwidth causing model stalls, and misconfigured autoscaling policies that either burst too aggressively or not at all. we provide a preflight checklist to avoid the usual pitfalls.
[07:10] Daniel Ortega: any legal or compliance hurdles we should anticipate when reselling?

[07:15] Sofia Kline: main items: DPA/SCCs for eu, clarity on data handling for regulated customers, and for reseller deals we include a clause about customer support SLAs. our legal team can do a redline pass.
[07:30] Jake Morales: on integration mechanics - would we run the redwood control plane in our environment or link to your control plane?

[07:36] Maya Chen: flexible - small partners often use our hosted control plane with dedicated capacity; larger partners or regulated customers put the control plane in their VPC. hybrid modes are possible where telemetry is sent to partner logs but orchestration remains in redwood.
[07:55] Priya Nair: about billing - we need a clear mapping of usage metrics if we're reselling so we can invoice end customers. do you expose per-token and per-embedding metering?

[08:03] Ravi Patel: yes. our billing exposes per-token generation, embedding units, and also committed capacity charges. for partners we can provide a partner usage API or weekly CSVs for reconciliation.
[08:20] Daniel Ortega: any required partner enablement sessions?
[08:23] Sofia Kline: we do partner onboarding workshops: technical, security, and GTM. usually two half-day sessions. we'll schedule those after the agreement.
[08:35] Jake Morales: can we co-brand the offering? some customers prefer a single vendor relationship.
[08:39] Sofia Kline: yes co-branding and white-label options exist for certain tiers. we'll include details in the partner deck.
[08:48] Priya Nair: ok let's talk about the benchmark plan quickly - ravi, you mentioned 3 model families. any specifics?

[08:54] Ravi Patel: suggested: a 7B chat model (low-latency), a 30B decoder for longer completions, and an embeddings model that we can use for a small retrieval demo. send us a test pool with drivers and we'll run for 48 hours. expected artifacts: latency percentiles, throughput, and per-token cost estimates.
[09:20] Elena Wu: how do you handle PII redaction and inference-time filtering?

[09:25] Maya Chen: we offer preprocessing hooks and optional request scrubbing; customers can plug their own redactors before payload hits the model. we can also sample redacted vs raw logs depending on the contract.
[09:40] Daniel Ortega: ok that all makes sense. anyone else have burning questions?
[09:45] Jake Morales: one last - how do you measure model regression risk when upgrading models?

[09:49] Ravi Patel: we tie rollouts to eval sets and production prompt sets; we run A/B tests and quality monitoring with regression alerts. rollbacks are automated if quality drops below threshold. we also support canary traffic routing.

[10:05] Sofia Kline: great - summary recap: we'll send partner deck + partner program doc; lumenforge will share GPU inventory and region list; ravi/maya will propose benchmark plan and we schedule a technical deep dive. any objections?
[10:18] Priya Nair: no objections. we'll target early feb for the deep-dive.
[10:23] Daniel Ortega: thanks everyone. look forward to the deck and the next steps.
[10:28] Sofia Kline: thanks all - i'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. have a great day.
